questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. **

Delhi had been captured, ransacked and rebuilt several (1)/ times and modern Delhi is a cluster of a number (2)/ of cities spread across the metropolitan region. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Option 1)__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Delhi has been' **should be there in place of **'Delhi had been'**
 
• The present perfect is a verb tense which is used to show that an action has taken place once or many times before now. The present perfect is most frequently used to talk about experiences or changes that have taken place, but there are other less common uses as well.
 
• Since we are talking about Delhi the above-mentioned actions happened sometime in the past but Delhi is still evolving and is now a cluster of cities, hence the action is still in progress, therefore "has been" is the most appropriate.
 
• So, present perfect will be more accurate to use here.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ransacked **means go through (a place) stealing things and causing damage 
 
• **Cluster **means a group of similar things or people positioned or occurring closely together
 
• **Across **is a preposition which means from one side to the other of (a place, area, etc.)

​**Thus, the correct sentence is:*** **Delhi has been captured, ransacked, and rebuilt several times and modern Delhi is a cluster of a number of cities spread across the metropolitan region.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence ****given**** with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

The closure ________ the workers adversely.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Affected.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

__
 
• In the above given blank, **'affected'** will be used.
 
• The closing of a shop or factory would have a **harmful** **impact** on its workers, who will lose their jobs.
 
• **Adverse***(adjective)* - preventing success or development; harmful; unfavourable.
 
 
• For Example - Taxes are having an **adverse **effect on production.
 
 
 
• **Affected***(adjective)* - influenced or touched by an external factor.
 
 
• For Example - It gave her a strange sense of loss that **affected **her more than she wanted to admit.
 
 
 
• The sentence tells that the workers will be influenced by the closure in a harmful way.
 
• Thus, **'affected'** is the most appropriate option.

**Therefore, the correct sentence is** *The closure **affected **the workers adversely.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• Let's look at the **meaning **of the other options:- 

 
 
• **Expected** = believed that something will happen.
 
• **Effected** = caused to come into being
 
• **Accept** = believed to be correct.

Many people look down upon

questions.solution:

questions.question:
A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.

She expects good news.

options.text: Good news is expected by her.
News should be good by her.
Good news was expected by her.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1315b0ed28cca1c7d8a1844355c4427c5e357e2a736f187b995f94d26e2633fc.png] **__Explanation:__**

The given sentence is given in active voice to convert it into passive voice, the following changes should be done:

 
• While converting the voice, subject, and object to change their places.
 
 
• 'Good news' is an object in an active voice that becomes the subject in the passive voice.
 
• 'She' which is a subject in the active voice becomes 'her' (objective case) object in passive voice.
 
 
 
• Simple present tense in active voice becomes (is + V₃) in passive voice.
 
• The preposition 'by' is introduced before the 'object'

**Thus, the sentence becomes: ***Good news is expected by her.*

questions.question:
A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.

“Do you write with a left hand?” she asked.

options.text: She asked whether I wrote with a left hand.
She asked that did I wrote with a left hand.
She ask if I write with my left hand.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**She asked whether I wrote with a left hand.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The above-given sentence is a question-sentence. Such a question can be answered by saying only 'Yes' or 'No'.
 
• To make an indirect speech of such questions, the word 'if' or 'whether' will be used in indirect speech.
 
• Both the words 'if' and 'whether' can be used interchangeably.
 
• Question mark (?) will not be used in the indirect speech of interrogative sentences.
 
• The question sentence will be expressed in assertive or positive form instead of interrogative form in the indirect speech i.e. helping verb will come after subject
 
• **Present Indefinite tense **in direct speech is changed into **past indefinite tense **in indirect speech.
 
• Hence, from the above rules option 1) i.e. *She asked whether I wrote with left hand *is the correct answer.

questions.question: Burman remembers that the cricket match is after 19th July but before 22nd July, while Sumit remembers that the cricket match is before 25th July but after 20th July. On which date of July is the cricket match?

Burman remembers that the cricket match is after 19th July but before 22nd July.

Possible dates accordingly is20th or 21st July

Sumit remembers that the cricket match is before 25th July but after 20th July.

Possible dates accordingly is 21st, 22nd, 23rd and 24th July

Common date between possible dates is 21 st July.

Hence, the correct answer is 21st July.

questions.question:
The following equation is incorrect. Which two signs should be interchanged to correct the equation?

9 ÷ 3 - 30 x 7 + 6 = 15
questions.solution:
1) + and ÷ → 9 + 3 - 30 × 7 ÷ 6 = 23 ≠15

2) - and + → 9 ÷ 3 + 30 × 7 - 6 = 207 ≠15

3) + and x → 9 ÷ 3 - 30 + 7 × 6 = 15

4) ÷ and x → 9 × 3 - 30 ÷ 7 + 6 = 28.71 ≠15

Hence, interchanging + and × gives the correct equation.

questions.question: If 7*7 = 140, 6*1 = 70 and 3*5 = 80, then ﬁnd the value of 4*4 = ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed is:

7*7 = (7 + 7) × 10 = 140

6*1 = (6 + 1) × 10 = 70

3*5 = (3 + 5) × 10 = 80

Similarly,

4*4 = (4 + 4) × 10 = 80

Hence, the correct answer is 80.

**Detailed solution:-**

Let Vaibhav’s age = a and Amit’s age = 5 + a

⇒ a = 16

questions.question: The incomes of S and T are in the ratio 3 : 4 and their expenditures are in the ratio 1 : 1. If S saves Rs. 4000 and T saves Rs. 22000, then what will be the income (in Rs.) of S?

Saving of S = Income of S – Expenditure of S

⇒ 4000 = 3a – b ----(1)

Saving of T = Income of T – Expenditure of T

⇒ 22000 = 4a – b ----(2)

⇒ 22000 – 4000 = 4a – 3a – b + b

⇒ 18000 = a

∴ Income of S = 3a = 3 × 18000 = 54000

Two pipes P and Q can ﬁll an empty tank in 25 hours and 20 hours respectively. Pipe R alone can empty the completely ﬁlled tank in 50 hours. Firstly both the pipes P and Q are opened and after 8 hours pipe R is also opened. What will be the total time (in hours) taken to completely ﬁll the tank?
questions.solution:
Time taken by pipe P to fill the tank = 25 hours

Time taken by pipe Q to fill the tank = 20 hours

Time taken by pipe R to empty the tank = 50 hours

Total capacity of tank = Lcm of (25, 20 and 50) = 100 units

Efficiency of pipe P = 100/25 = 4 units/hour

Efficiency of pipe Q = 100/20 = 5 units/hour

Efficiency of pipe Q = – 100/50 = – 2 units/hour

Efficiency of pipe P and Q together = 5 + 4 = 9 units/hour

Efficiency of pipe P, Q and R together = 5 + 4 – 2 = 7 units/hour

Tank filled in 8 hours = 9 × 8 = 72 units

Remaining capacity = 100 – 72 = 28 units

Time taken to fill remaining 28 units = 28/7 = 4 hours

∴ Total time taken to fill the tank = 8 + 4 = 12 h

• It was launched by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The European planters at Champaran in Bihar practised indigo cultivation through illegal methods and forced the Indian farmers to cultivate Indigo on 3/20th part of their land. This was called Tinkathia system.
 
• This natural Indigo was used to make dye. The Germans, by then, had invented the way to make artificial dye because of which the demand for natural Indigo fell.
 
• Now, if the farmers wished to shift to cultivate other crops, they could do so only by paying large amount of ‘compensation’ or ‘tawan’.
 
• Thus, Champaran’s peasants with the help of Gandhi Ji and Rajendra Prasad organized Champaran Satyagraha and abolished Tinkathia system (1919).

questions.question:
Generally covalently bonded molecules ________.

I. Have high boiling and melting point as compared to ionically bonded molecules

II. Are poor conductors of electricity.

III. Have weak inter-molecular force.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II and III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Covalent Bond:**

 
 
• **A type of chemical bond wherein two or more atoms share one or more electron pairs.**
 
• The outer shell of each has crossed over the other,
 
• Each atom shares its valence electron with the other atom.
 
• It can be said as an electrostatic force of attraction between two or more atoms or molecules.
 
• There are two types of covalent bonds - sigma and pi bonds.
 
• Sigma is the strongest covalent bond while pi-bond is the weakest covalent bond.
 
 
 
• Sigma and Pi bonds:-
 
 
• The overlapping of atomic orbitals distinguishes the **sigma and pi bonds from each other.**
 
• The overlapping of atomic orbitals forms covalent bonds.
 
• The head-to-head overlapping of atomic orbitals forms sigma bonds, whereas the lateral overlap of two atomic orbitals forms pi bonds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Covalently bonded compounds do not have free electrons, so they do not conduct electric current.​ 
 
• Covalently bonded molecules have low melting and boiling points because intermolecular forces are weak and little amount of energy is required to break the forces.
 
• If the compounds have high melting and boiling point then they have very strong or strong intermolecular forces. 
 
• If compounds have medium melting and boiling point then they have medium intermolecular forces.
 
• The intermolecular forces between water molecules are stronger than those between oxygen molecules.
 
• Covalent bonds are formed by the mutual sharing of electrons.
 
• Hence the covalently bonded molecules have strong bonds within the molecule.

questions.question: Who summons the joint sitting of both the houses of the Indian Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option __**2**__ i.e __**President of India**__.

__
 
• According to Article 108 of the Indian constitution, the joint sitting of the Parliament is called by the President__.
 
• It is presided over by the Speaker or, in his absence, by the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha or in his absence, the Deputy-Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Joint session of Parliament can be summoned in the following situations -
 
 
• If after a Bill has been passed by one House and submitted to the other House and the Bill is rejected by the other House.
 
• The Houses have finally disagreed as to the amendments to be made in the Bill.
 
• More than six months elapse from the date of the reception of the Bill by the other House without the Bill being passed by it.
 
 
 
• The President may, unless the Bill has elapsed by reason of a dissolution of the House of the People, notify to the Houses by message if they are sitting or by public notification if they are not sitting, his intention to summon them to meet in a joint sitting for the purpose of deliberating and voting on the Bill.

questions.question: Who expanded the cell theory and suggested that all the cells arise from pre-existing cells?

questions.question: Find the acceleration (in m/s²) produced in a body of mass 10 kg when a force of 20 N is applied on it
questions.solution:
The acceleration (in m/s2) produced in a body of mass 10 kg when a force of 20 N is applied on it is 2 m/s².

 
• The formula for force: force = mass × acceleration.
 
• Therefore acceleration = force ÷ mass.
 
• Here acceleration = 20 ÷ 10 = 2 m/s².

questions.question: The product of mass of a body and the acceleration produced in it equals the _________ acting on it.
questions.solution:
The product of the mass of a body and the acceleration produced in it equals the Force acting on it.

• Force: It is those physical quantities that are defined as the push or pull of an object.

 
 
• Its unit is Newton.
 
 

Equation of Force:

⇒ F = ma

Where m is the mass and a is the acceleration of the body

questions.question: The process of transferring of charge from a charged object to the earth is called ________.
questions.solution:
The process of transferring of charge from a charged object to the earth is called Earthing.

__
 
• Importance of Earthing:
 
 
• It protects human lives by providing safety to electrical appliances from leakage of current.
 
• It protects buildings form lighting.
 
• It removes the risk of fire in electrical systems.
 
 

Explanation:__

There are two types of charges found in nature -

 
• Positive charge
 
• Negative charge

Properties of charges:

 
• Like charges (same charges) repel each other.
 
• Unlike charges (different charges) attract each other.
 
• When two objects are rubbed against each other, they develop charges.
 
• Earthing: The process of transfer of charge from a charged object to the Earth is known as Earthing.
 
• Lightning is caused because of the build-up of electrostatic charges in the clouds.
 
• Lightning Conductor: It is a device used to protect buildings from the effect of lightning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/925f01df4e3ec65250564381709186f9ad472eb76c3f879f6b9cc978e01e0109.png] 

 
• A metallic rod, taller than the building, is installed in the walls of the building during its construction.
 
• One end of the rod is kept out in the air and the other is buried deep in the ground.
 
• The rod provides an easy route for the transfer of electric charge to the ground.
 
• Copper is used because it is a good conductor of electricity.
 
• The lightning conductor is sharp-pointed because this will ensure a high electric field and hence the quick flow of electric charges to the ground.
